content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To clean jet, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Remove engine inlet covers (10 minutes)
Step 2. Apply chemical degreaser to landing gear (45 minutes)
Step 3. Hand-scrub the vertical stabilizer (2 hours)
Step 4. Polish the cockpit canopy glass (1 hour)
Step 5. Position the heavy-duty mobile scaffolding (30 minutes)
Step 6. Power-wash the wheel wells (20 minutes)
Step 7. Mix the specialized aviation soap solution (15 minutes)
Step 8. Rinse the fuselage with deionized water (40 minutes)
Step 9. Spray down the wings and flaps (30 minutes)
Step 10. Inspect the exterior for oil leaks (1 hour)
Step 11. Tape off sensitive static ports and sensors (25 minutes)
Step 12. Scrub the underside of the fuselage (3 hours)
Step 13. Apply corrosion inhibitor to exposed joints (1.5 hours)
Step 14. Document the pre-wash maintenance state (20 minutes)
Step 15. Disconnect external ground power (5 minutes)
Step 16. Steam clean the brake assemblies (50 minutes)
Step 17. Wipe down the engine cowlings (40 minutes)
Step 18. Scrub the belly of the aircraft (2 hours)
Step 19. Clear debris from the runway work area (15 minutes)
Step 20. Apply protective wax to the leading edges (4 hours)
Step 21. Remove protective tape from sensors (10 minutes)
Step 22. Detail the nose cone and radar dome (1 hour)
Step 23. Prepare the high-pressure water system (20 minutes)
Step 24. Set up water reclamation mats (35 minutes)
Step 25. Clean the navigation light lenses (15 minutes)
Step 26. Degrease the hydraulic lines (1 hour)
Step 27. Check the pitot tube covers (5 minutes)
Step 28. Wash the horizontal stabilizers (1.5 hours)
Step 29. Tow the jet to the drying hangar (30 minutes)
Step 30. Blow-dry the rivets and seams with compressed air (2 hours)
Step 31. Buff the exterior paint to a high shine (6 hours)
Step 32. Inspect the upper wing surfaces (45 minutes)
Step 33. Clear the hangar of unnecessary equipment (1 hour)
Step 34. Seal the passenger door seams (15 minutes)
Step 35. Lubricate the landing gear struts (30 minutes)
Step 36. Apply anti-icing fluid to the tail (1 hour)
Step 37. Conduct a safety walk-around of the perimeter (20 minutes)
Step 38. Final inspection of the landing gear bay (30 minutes)
Step 39. Re-install the engine covers for storage (15 minutes)
Step 40. Sign off on the cleaning logbook (5 minutes)
